title: NeoPixel Remote
intro: Slide sliders on a web page to change the colours of a NeoPixel strip.

steps.title: Light the strip
steps.text:
A NeoPixel strip is a row of tiny lights. Each one mixes **red, green and blue**, from 0 (off) to 255 (full).

**Your task:** change `fillStrip(0, 0, 255)` to make purple (lots of red and blue), then Run.
hints: The three numbers are red, green and blue.
Purple is red and blue together.

checks.label: It's not plain blue any more

steps.success: Every colour on a screen is made by mixing red, green and blue, just like this.

steps.title: Sliders on your phone
steps.text:
The page has three **sliders** in a **form**. Pressing **Light up!** opens an address like `/colour?r=255&g=0&b=100`. `server.arg("r")` gets the number after `r=`.

Your board makes its **own WiFi network** (a hotspot). On your phone, open WiFi settings, join the network with your board's name, then open **192.168.4.1** in the browser. In the simulator, use the **phone panel**.

**Your task:** fill in the blanks to read green and blue too.
hints: Each slider has a `name` in the HTML.
steps.success: A colour remote on your phone!

steps.title: Party mode
steps.text: **Goal:** add a **Party** button on the page (a link to `/party`) that makes the strip flash 10 random colours, then go back to the last colour picked.
hints: Keep the last colour in global variables, so `party()` can go back to it.
steps.success: Party mode! You added a whole new feature to your web page.

outro: Your web page sends numbers to the board in the **address** (like `/colour?r=255&g=0&b=100`), and the board mixes them into light. Web forms everywhere work like this.
stretch: Add a Rainbow button that runs a rainbow animation.
Remember the last colour and show it on the sliders when the page opens.
